newsitem.title: FRANCE: French shopowners union leader gets year in jail.
newsitem.headline: French shopowners union leader gets year in jail.

text.p: The leader of a right-wing shop owners' union whose arrest triggered violent protests in this southern France town was sentenced on Tuesday to a year in jail for fraud and threatening a judge's life.

Christian Poncet automatically faces a further two years jail due to an earlier conviction on separate charges which had been suspended. In the event of a new jail sentence in France, an earlier suspended sentence is automatically added on.
Poncet admitted at his trial that he physically threatened the magistrate but said the threats made no mention of death.
His detention at the weekend ahead of the trial had sparked violent clashes between hundreds of his backers and police who used tear gas and arrested a dozen demonstrators.
Poncet is a national leader of the rightist Confederation for the Defence of Shop Owners and Artisans (CDCA)
